clue.text: Charlie, Benny, and Jimmy, perhaps, getting colds

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Benny Hill the comedian and Jimmy Hill the football presenter are both Hills

explanation.surface: Three men named Charlie, Benny and Jimmy all coming down with colds at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian and Jimmy Hill a British football broadcaster; 'perhaps' marks them as examples of the surname, and Charlie is the alphabet code word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shivery fits and mild colds are both called chills in everyday speech.

clue.text: Run married women's quarters

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: An instruction to run the living quarters of the married women.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a harem is the secluded part of a household set aside for the wives and concubines.

clue.text: Returning to fight off outcast

indicators.note: returning says the word for the phrase to fight off is read backwards

parts.note: to repel an attacker is to fight them off

explanation.surface: Coming back to drive away a person shunned by everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person with leprosy was shunned, so the word has come to mean any social outcast.

clue.text: Maliciously restrained by self-styled inspector from the south

indicators.note: from the south says the hidden letters are read backwards
restrained by says the letters are held within the words self-styled inspector

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A self-appointed inspector keeping someone in check out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Maliciously restrained' as the definition, but 'restrained by' is the hiding signal; the definition is 'Maliciously' alone. YLEDINS, read upwards ('from the south'), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting snidely means acting with sly, spiteful malice.

clue.text: Inappropriately employing young woman to welcome Union leader with gin shot

indicators.note: to welcome means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a miss is a young unmarried woman

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of Union
shot in the sense of wrecked or broken signals the letters of gin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl greeting a trade union boss with a measure of gin, which is not what she should be doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a measure of spirit but it rearranges GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to misuse something is to employ it wrongly or for the wrong purpose.

clue.text: One of Tati's masterpieces? Not originally released, it's in the eye of the beholder

definitions.text: it's in the eye of the beholder

indicators.note: released means let go, so a letter is set free from the title

parts.note: Mon Oncle is a celebrated 1958 film by the French director Jacques Tati

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Not

explanation.surface: Praise of a Tati film that was never put out, with beauty in the eye of the beholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' looks like a film release, but it takes N (first of 'Not') out of MON ONCLE. The definition plays on the saying: a single eyeglass sits in its wearer's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: a single lens worn screwed into one eye socket is literally lodged in the eye of whoever is looking.

clue.text: More sporadic fights over half of beer

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice

indicators.note: half of takes the back two of the four letters of beer

explanation.surface: Fights breaking out less often over half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sparser means thinner on the ground, scattered and occurring at wider intervals.

clue.text: Picts: one's designed one of their national symbols?

indicators.note: designed means made up or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The ancient Picts creating one of their own national emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were early people of Scotland, so 'their' points to the Scots; the anagram of PICTS ONES gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this native conifer is widely regarded as the national tree of Scotland.

clue.text: If nude, I'll somehow be rendered ineffective

indicators.note: somehow means in some unexplained way, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fearing that going naked will leave them powerless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ruling or effort that has been nullified has been cancelled or made void.

clue.text: Top up with urine? That's rash

indicators.note: up in the sense of in disorder signals the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A foolish suggestion to refill something with urine, dismissed as reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective for reckless, but it is the skin complaint; 'up' shuffles TOP and URINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a skin rash is an outbreak of spots, which doctors call an eruption.

clue.text: A striking face and stout heart make for handsome youth

parts.note: the poll is the flat striking end of a hammer head

indicators.note: heart picks the central letter of the word stout

explanation.surface: A striking face and a brave heart are the makings of a good-looking young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout heart' suggests courage, but 'heart' just takes the middle of STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the Greek god of light was the classical ideal of youthful male beauty.

clue.text: One escapes from crises in Arrivals

indicators.note: escapes from says a letter leaves the word for crises

parts.note: crises and emergencies are synonyms
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone getting free of trouble in an airport arrivals hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrivals' looks like the airport area but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an arrival is a coming into view, just as each emerging is an appearance.

clue.text: Violently eject 50% of faeces out of sump

indicators.note: out of picks the outside letters of the word sump
50% of takes the back half of the four-letter word

parts.note: faeces is the formal word for the vulgar shit

explanation.surface: A grim scene of sewage being forced up out of a drain sump.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spit is to expel something forcibly from the mouth.

clue.text: It's grotesque to use mouthwash to entertain young male with shaved head

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to gargle is to rinse the throat with mouthwash

indicators.note: a shaved head loses its top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A skinhead lad being treated to a gargle, which is a grotesque scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesque' is a noun here: a carved figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in architecture a grotesque is a carved distorted figure, and a spouting one on a church is the classic example.

clue.text: A little application and skill required to make a sweet treat

parts.note: an applet is a small software application
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A modest effort and some skill are all you need to bake a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fruit-filled pastry dessert is a classic sweet treat.

clue.text: Historic county in Vogue?

definitions.meaning: a former county of south Wales, now split into smaller authorities
split as ..., a publication about glamour, which describes the fashion magazine

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split after its fourth letter: GLAM plus ORGAN, a periodical, which is what the magazine Vogue is; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Welsh county containing Cardiff was abolished as an administrative area in 1974.

clue.text: God's present: fruit

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god, and 's stands for is
in means present, as in the doctor is in

explanation.surface: A deity's gift to humankind turns out to be fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God's present' reads as a gift; split it as RA IS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dried grape is a fruit, eaten as it is or in cakes.

clue.text: Second crash happened unexpectedly

parts.note: a prang is British slang for a minor car crash

explanation.surface: A second car accident occurring out of the blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that sprang up arose suddenly and without warning.

clue.text: Get to grips with Greek technology company

parts.note: Apple is the technology company behind the iPhone

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a Greek tech firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to grapple with a problem is to wrestle with it, literally to seize hold.

clue.text: Had a nice cocktail in famous nightclub

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Enjoying a good mixed drink at a well-known club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hacienda was a celebrated Manchester nightclub of the acid-house era.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Manchester club run by Factory Records became a byword for the rave scene.

clue.text: Things spiral as hell nearly freezes over

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another comes first
nearly drops the final letter of hell

parts.note: ices means freezes

explanation.surface: Things go into a spin because hell is close to freezing over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freezes over' looks like the idiom for never, but 'over' places the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: coils and screw threads are spiral things, which in geometry are helixes.

clue.text: Agree with beginning to restrain a monster

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of restrain

explanation.surface: Agreeing to begin holding a monster back.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Greek myth the fire-breathing beast with lion, goat and serpent parts is a monster.

clue.text: Heard urgent call to release bricks

indicators.note: heard says the clue words are said out loud

parts.note: let go is the shout to make someone release a hold

explanation.surface: Someone shouting to drop the bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Danish toy is a system of plastic interlocking building bricks.

clue.text: Fifty involved in perverted lathering session that goes on until dawn

definitions.text: session that goes on until dawn

indicators.note: involved in says one piece is caught up inside the other
perverted means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people at a kinky soapy party that runs all night.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an all-night study, work or party session is called by this informal name.

clue.text: Former tennis player loses a point to become the most powerful person in the universe?

definitions.text: the most powerful person in the universe?

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the player

parts.note: Tim Henman was a leading British tennis player
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A retired tennis star dropping a point and somehow becoming all-powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the cartoon hero's billing as the most powerful man in the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the 1980s cartoon muscleman was billed as the strongest man in the universe.

clue.text: Opposition fighters to be sent back, in case of emergency

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
the case of a word is its outside letters
to be sent back says the word for fighters is turned round

parts.note: men are soldiers, fighters in the ranks

explanation.surface: Hostile troops to be returned if there is an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the opposing side in a war is the foe, the other side.

clue.text: Display preoccupation

definitions.meaning: to hang a picture up is to display it
an emotional fixation or neurosis, informally

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hang-up is a nagging worry, and to hang something up is to put it on show.

clue.text: Top tip to tantalise with each afternoon meal

parts.note: the cream rises to the top of milk, and the cream of anything is its best

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advice on teasing someone with each treat at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British meal of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tea with scones, jam and clotted cream is a traditional English afternoon meal.

clue.text: They are very smelly, small mischievous children

parts.note: a tinker is British slang for a naughty child

explanation.surface: Little rascals who smell awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinker' is everyday British for a cheeky, mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things that reek are informally said to stink, and each one is a stinker.

clue.text: Maybe a report on the radio irritates

indicators.note: on the radio means spoken over the air, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a report such as a gunshot is an example of a noise

explanation.surface: A news report broadcast on the radio gets on someone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a news item but is a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to irritate someone is to bother or vex them.
